hero.name: Tadashi (CHU)
hero.tagline: Student at the University of Aizu. Backend engineering as my core — with machine learning, deep learning, and LLM work woven in.

about.title: A little about me
body: I'm Tadashi — a CS student at the University of Aizu in Fukushima, currently interning at 2WINS, Inc. My main focus is backend engineering — designing APIs, data layers, and the plumbing that keeps a product running — but I also work as a machine learning engineer, wiring models and LLM pipelines into real applications. What keeps pulling me back to this field is the gap between a paper and a product — closing it means understanding the math well enough to reimplement it, and the engineering well enough to make it serve someone.

I tend to learn by rebuilding. Backend work I mostly learn on the job — designing APIs, wrangling data layers, fixing bugs that only surface under load. On the ML side my public side-projects are from-scratch studies: a mini GPT in pure PyTorch, the "Deep Learning from Scratch" book redone in NumPy, classical and deep-learning pipelines benchmarked side by side. When I'm not shipping or studying, I'm usually on Kaggle, reading a paper, or chasing a footnote someone else would've skipped.

howIWork.title: A few things I try to do

principles.title: Reimplement to understand.
principles.body: If I can't rebuild it, I don't really know it.

principles.title: Compare before committing.
principles.body: Classical baselines alongside deep learning — I pick a direction only after I've seen them race.

principles.title: Ship it, then improve it.
principles.body: A rough version in production teaches more than a polished one in a notebook.

principles.title: Learn the plumbing too.
principles.body: Caching, async, data wrangling — the unglamorous parts decide whether a model ever ships.

capabilities.title: Backend services & APIs.
capabilities.body: Designing and shipping async APIs on FastAPI + PostgreSQL — SQLModel, Alembic migrations, auth, pytest / Playwright coverage, and Docker / AWS deploys.

capabilities.title: Full-stack product features.
capabilities.body: TypeScript frontends (SvelteKit / React + Tailwind) wired into my Python backends, end to end.

capabilities.title: LLM-powered features.
capabilities.body: Prompt engineering, structured output, and pipeline work with LangChain and commercial LLM APIs.

capabilities.title: ML / DL from scratch.
capabilities.body: Transformers, CNNs, and classical baselines in PyTorch and NumPy — built from the paper up, not just wrapped.
